Mahindra is the grandson of [[Jagdish Chandra Mahindra]], co-founder of [[Mahindra & Mahindra]]. As of 2023, his net worth according to [[Forbes]] was estimated to be $2.1 billion.{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/anand-mahindra/|title=Forbes profile: Anand Mahindra|website=www.forbes.com|access-date=29 April 2021|archive-date=2 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602212942/https://www.forbes.com/profile/anand-mahindra/|url-status=live}} He is an alumnus of [[Harvard University]] and [[Harvard Business School]]. In 1996, he established Nanhi Kali, a non-government organisation that supports education for underprivileged girls in India. He is included by [[Fortune Magazine]] among the 'World's 50 Greatest Leaders',{{cite web|url=https://money.cnn.com/gallery/leadership/2014/03/20/worlds-best-leaders.fortune/40.html|title=Fortune ranks the World's 50 Greatest Leaders|work=Fortune |publisher=CNN Money|access-date=2 July 2014|archive-date=23 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140323130713/http://money.cnn.com/gallery/leadership/2014/03/20/worlds-best-leaders.fortune/40.html|url-status=dead |last1=Colvin |first1=Geoff }} and was in the magazine's 2011 listing of Asia's 25 most powerful businesspeople.{{cite web|url=https://money.cnn.com/galleries/2011/news/international/1104/gallery.asia_most_powerful.fortune/25.html|title=25 most powerful businesspeople in Asia|publisher=CNN Money|access-date=2 July 2014|archive-date=18 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318092808/http://money.cnn.com/galleries/2011/news/international/1104/gallery.asia_most_powerful.fortune/25.html|url-status=dead}} Anand was noted by [[Forbes (India)]] as their 'Entrepreneur of the Year' for 2013.{{cite web|url=http://forbesindia.com/article/special/anand-mahindra-is-forbes-india-entrepreneur-for-the-year-2013/36323/1|title=anand mahindra is forbes india entrepreneur for the year|publisher=CNN Money|access-date=2 July 2014|archive-date=17 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140917175424/http://forbesindia.com/article/special/anand-mahindra-is-forbes-india-entrepreneur-for-the-year-2013/36323/1|url-status=dead}} He was given the [[Padma Bhushan]] Award, the third highest civilian award in India, in January 2020.{{cite web | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/anand-mahindra-venu-srinivasan-to-be-honoured-with-padma-bhushan-naukri-com-founder-to-get-padma-shri/articleshow/73628195.cms | title=Anand Mahindra, Venu Srinivasan to be honoured with Padma Bhushan; Anuja Sharma and Radhika Nath.{{Cite web|url=http://harvardmagazine.com/2011/04/to-think-and-to-question|title=To Think and to Question|date=27 April 2011|website=harvardmagazine.com}} He completed his early schooling from [[Lawrence School, Lovedale|Lawrence School]], [[Lovedale, India|Lovedale]]{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/kabaddi-deserves-a-league-of-its-own-anand-mahindra/articleshow/33536965.cms|title=Kabaddi deserves a league of its own: Anand Mahindra|date=10 April 2014|website=Economic Times|access-date=16 October 2017|archive-date=2 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602222923/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/magazines/panache/kabaddi-deserves-a-league-of-its-own-anand-mahindra/articleshow/33536965.cms|url-status=live}} and then went on to study film making and architecture from [[Harvard University]] where he graduated magna cum laude in 1977. In 1981, he completed his MBA from the [[Harvard Business School]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.alumni.hbs.edu/stories/Pages/story-bulletin.aspx?num=1994|title=ANAND G. MAHINDRA, MBA 1981|date=1 January 2008|website=Alumni|access-date=16 October 2017|archive-date=12 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171012151256/https://www.alumni.hbs.edu/stories/Pages/story-bulletin.aspx?num=1994|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/cover-story/anand-mahindra-mandm-company-acquisitions/story/18656.html|title=Top gun|date=2 October 2011|website=Business Today|access-date=16 October 2017|archive-date=13 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171013230051/http://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/cover-story/anand-mahindra-mandm-company-acquisitions/story/18656.html|url-status=live}} ==Career== In 1981, Anand joined [[Mahindra Ugine Steel|Mahindra Ugine Steel Company Ltd (MUSCO)]] as an Executive Assistant to the Finance Director.{{Citation needed|date=June 2021}} In 1989 he was appointed President and Deputy Managing Director of MUSCO. He initiated the Mahindra Group's diversification into new business areas of real estate development and hospitality management.{{cite web|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/elite/profile/anand-mahindra-827.html|title=Anand Mahindra|publisher=Money Control|access-date=24 October 2017|archive-date=24 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024154904/http://www.moneycontrol.com/elite/profile/anand-mahindra-827.html|url-status=live}} On 4 April 1991, he took the role of Deputy Managing Director of [[Mahindra & Mahindra]] Ltd., a producer of off-road vehicles and agricultural tractors in India. In April 1997, Anand was appointed the Managing Director and in 2001 the Vice Chairman of Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd.{{cite web|url= https://www.reuters.com/finance/stocks/company-officers/MAHM.BO|title=Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd (MAHM.BO)| publisher=Reuters|access-date=24 October 2017}} In August 2012, he took on the role of Chairman of the board and Managing Director of the Mahindra Group from his uncle, [[Keshub Mahindra]].{{cite web|url=https://finapp.co.in/anand-mahindra-net-worth/|title=Anand Mahindra Net Worth (House Cars Salary Income 2017)|publisher=finapp|access-date=24 October 2017|archive-date=16 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016175713/https://finapp.co.in/anand-mahindra-net-worth/|url-status=live}} In November 2016, Anand was re-designated as Executive Chairman of Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd and continued to be the Chairman of [[Mahindra Group]].{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/cC7EUvGzILDU0KpYF0adyK/Mahindra-appoints-Anand-Mahindra-as-executive-chairman-Q2-p.html|title=Pawan Goenka named MD of Mahindra; Anand Mahindra to be executive chairman|publisher=Livemint|date=11 November 2016|access-date=13 October 2017|archive-date=4 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104204511/https://www.livemint.com/Companies/cC7EUvGzILDU0KpYF0adyK/Mahindra-appoints-Anand-Mahindra-as-executive-chairman-Q2-p.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url= https://auto.ndtv.com/news/what-anand-mahindra-had-to-say-about-tata-motors-10-000-electric-car-order-1757094|title= What Anand Mahindra Had To Say About Tata Motors' 10,000 Electric Car Order|publisher= NDTV Auto|date= 30 September 2017|access-date= 24 October 2017|archive-date= 24 October 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171024153305/https://auto.ndtv.com/news/what-anand-mahindra-had-to-say-about-tata-motors-10-000-electric-car-order-1757094|url-status= live}} Anand was a co-promoter of [[Kotak Mahindra Bank]] (formally known as Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd.). life == Anand married Anuradha, who was a journalist and later launched the magazine ''[[Verve (Indian magazine)|Verve]]''. She is currently the editor of magazines Verve and [[MW (Indian magazine)|Man's World]]. Anand Gopal Mahindra (born 1 May 1955) is an Indian billionaire businessman, and the chairman of Mahindra Group, a Mumbai-based business conglomerate. The group operates in aerospace, agribusiness, aftermarket, automotive, components, construction equipment, defence, energy, farm equipment, finance and insurance, industrial equipment, information technology, leisure and hospitality, logistics, real estate and retail. Mahindra is the grandson of Jagdish Chandra Mahindra, co-founder of Mahindra & Mahindra.
As of 2023, his net worth according to Forbes was estimated to be $2.1 billion. He is an alumnus of Harvard University and Harvard Business School. In 1996, he established Nanhi Kali, a non-government organisation that supports education for underprivileged girls in India.
He is included by Fortune Magazine among the 'World's 50 Greatest Leaders', and was in the magazine's 2011 listing of Asia's 25 most powerful businesspeople. Anand was noted by Forbes (India) as their 'Entrepreneur of the Year' for 2013. He was given the Padma Bhushan Award, the third highest civilian award in India, in January 2020.
As per Forbes list of India’s 100 richest tycoons, dated 9 October 2024, Anand Mahindra is ranked 80th with a net worth of $3.97 billion.
